title: Electric Circuits and Ohm's Law
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Electric Circuits and Ohm's Law Worksheets (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Electric current is the flow of electric charge: voltage, current and resistance, Ohm's law, series and parallel circuits, circuit diagrams, and AC and DC. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Science 9, Physics)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 science worksheets (BC): charge, current and voltage, circuit symbols, Ohm's law (V = IR), series and parallel circuits. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Series: one path. Parallel: more than one path.
body_html:
How to think about it

Current (I, in amperes) is the flow of charge. Voltage (V, in volts) is the energy each charge carries. Resistance (R, in ohms) opposes the current. Ohm's law: V = I × R. Batteries give direct current (DC); wall outlets give alternating current (AC).

In a series circuit there is one path: the current is the same everywhere and the voltages add up. In a parallel circuit there are several paths: the voltage across each branch is the same and the currents add up. If one bulb in series breaks, they all go out.

Example

A 12 V battery pushes 3 A through a resistor. What is its resistance?

R = V ÷ I

Answer: 4 Ω

Example

Why are houses wired in parallel?

One appliance off...

Answer: each device works on its own

Common mistakes

  • Thinking current is used up in a circuit.
  • Mixing up voltage and current.
  • Thinking adding bulbs in parallel makes them dimmer.

faq.a: It breaks the circuit if the current gets too high.

faq.q: Which kind of current comes from a wall outlet?
faq.a: Alternating current (AC), which changes direction many times a second.
